ArrCtrl checks your servers itself and tells you what\'s new. Nothing goes through any outside service.
Turned on, but Android is blocking ArrCtrl\'s notifications
Open Android\'s notification settings for ArrCtrl

Background checks can be delayed by Android, especially to save battery. With ntfy, your servers wake ArrCtrl the moment something happens; ArrCtrl then checks and notifies you. The README explains how to point each service at the address below.
Your servers wake ArrCtrl through the ntfy app
Needs the ntfy app, which isn\'t installed
Waiting for ntfy to give an address…
On. Give your servers the address below
ntfy couldn\'t register ArrCtrl (%1$s). Open ntfy once, then turn this on again.
ntfy temporarily unavailable: its server can\'t be reached. Your address stays the same, and background checks keep running.
Instant notifications come only through the ntfy app. Install it, then turn on Instant with ntfy. Background checks work without it.
Android can cut ntfy\'s connection while the phone sleeps, so wake-ups arrive late. Tap to open ntfy\'s App info and set Battery to Unrestricted.
Posts to the push address, like your servers will, so ArrCtrl checks straight away
Sent. “Last wake-up” updates when it arrives.
Couldn\'t reach the push address. Is your ntfy server reachable from this phone?
Each kind is also its own channel in Android\'s notification settings, where you can change its sound or how it appears.
Turn a server off to stop notifications from it.
A quiet, ongoing notification with what\'s downloading and how fast
Updates about once a minute while something downloads, and goes away when nothing does. This uses more battery, so it\'s off by default.
Android won\'t hold back ArrCtrl\'s checks to save battery
Android may delay checks for hours. Tap to let ArrCtrl run unrestricted

Some phones (OPPO and OnePlus with ColorOS, Xiaomi, Samsung, Huawei) also stop apps in the background on their own. If notifications arrive late, allow background activity and auto-launch for ArrCtrl in its app settings.

Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening ArrCtrl. While locked, your API keys and passwords stay encrypted with the PIN

ArrCtrl has no analytics or tracking. It only talks to your own servers. While ArrCtrl is locked, widgets keep showing what they last loaded and the Quick Settings tile opens the app; they refresh again once you unlock.
Screenshots and screen recordings show a blank screen
The recent apps view shows a blank card instead of the app
Couldn\'t unlock with your fingerprint. Use your PIN.
A fingerprint was added or removed. Unlock with your PIN, then turn fingerprint unlock on again.
Enter your PIN. It\'s needed after a restart and every 72 hours.
Too many tries. Try again in %1$d s

The PIN can\'t be recovered, because it encrypts your saved API keys and passwords. ArrCtrl will remove every server with its API key or password, and what the widgets and notifications remembered on this phone. Nothing changes on your servers.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN. If you forget it, the only way back in is to add your servers again.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN.
At least %1$d digits, separate from your phone\'s PIN
Enter your app PIN to turn the lock off.
Too easy to guess. Try a less obvious PIN.
The PINs didn\'t match. Start again.
Couldn\'t save the PIN. Try again.
Only strong biometrics such as your fingerprint, checked by the phone\'s secure hardware. The PIN is still needed after a restart and every 72 hours.
Set up a fingerprint on this phone first
As soon as you leave the app

Notifications are on, so background checks can still sign in while ArrCtrl is locked: your API keys and passwords are then only encrypted with the Android Keystore, as without the app lock, and widgets and the tile keep working. Turn off notifications to keep them sealed with your PIN too. ArrCtrl has no analytics or tracking.
